message.content: Although an Leshy, Pebble Spring became immediately fascinated by the mortal settlements when they set foot in a city. They loves the nicely paved ground, the intricate bridges, and the most of all, they loved houses. The nicely layed out stone walls forming shelters from the weathers yet connect the earth with the stories from every family. They decided to learn the craft of housebuilding with the help of a touch of arcane magic from their self-made staff. Pebble Spring visited the local carpenter's shop every day to watch the old craftsman measure and cut beams with precision. The wood shavings curled up in the air like tiny ribbons, and the Leshy found them mesmerizing. They would sit in the corner, tapping their staff against the floor while the master explained the fundamentals of framing. A sturdy wall required proper alignment, the carpenter said, otherwise the entire structure would collapse under the weight of winter storms. Pebble Spring nodded, absorbing every word with the patience of a creature who had seen forests grow over centuries. By the third week, the Leshy had memorized the angles needed for a gabled roof and the spacing between load-bearing posts. The arcane magic in their staff allowed the stones to bond together without mortar, a gift that impressed even the grumpiest mason in the district. Pebble Spring's first attempt was a small shed behind the tavern, built entirely from river-smoothed rocks and branches. The townsfolk gathered around to admire the little structure, which somehow looked like a cottage that had grown from the ground itself. They hummed with quiet pride as the rain tapped against the moss-covered roof they had so carefully shaped. Word spread quickly through the market square that a forest spirit was taking up residence in the old quarry district. Families began requesting small additions to their homes, and Pebble Spring accepted each project with genuine enthusiasm. The Leshy worked from dawn until dusk, their hands never tired, their magic steady and reliable. Neighbors brought baskets of berries and warm bread as tokens of gratitude for the new porches and fireplaces. Seasons turned, and the little houses that sprouted along the riverbanks became a beloved landmark of the town. Pebble Spring realized that building for others gave a deeper satisfaction than building for oneself. The Leshy began teaching young apprentices the basics of stone-cutting and timber joinery in the open workshop. Their students marveled at the way the staff could coax a boulder into perfect shape with a gentle tap. Each new structure carried a whisper of the old forest, a reminder that the earth and the people could share a roof. The pebble creature walked slowly through the narrow cobblestone alleys of the bustling old stone settlement, carefully observing how the local merchants arranged their colorful wares on weathered wooden stalls each bright morning, and spotty patterns of golden light filtered down through the hanging lanterns above.
